# Getting Started with Loom API v2.2

Welcome to Loom! This guide will walk you through making your first workflow execution using the Loom HTTP API. By the end, you'll have uploaded a workflow definition, started an execution, checked its status, and set up a webhook to receive completion notifications.

All examples use `curl` against the Loom API base URL:

```
https://api.loom.sh/v2
```

---

## 1. Get an API Key

Loom uses **scoped API keys** for authentication. Obtain a key from your Loom dashboard (or contact your administrator). You'll pass it in the `X-Loom-Key` header on every request.

> **Note:** OAuth2 support is planned but has not shipped yet. For now, API keys are the only authentication method for v2.

> **Legacy note:** If you're migrating from v1, the old `Authorization: Bearer <token>` scheme still works, but only on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix. For v2 endpoints, always use `X-Loom-Key`.

---

## 2. Upload a Workflow Definition

Workflows are defined as YAML or JSON documents and uploaded via `POST /workflows`. The maximum definition size is **1 MB**.

### Example: Upload a YAML workflow

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-yaml" \
  -d '
name: greet
steps:
  - id: say_hello
    action: echo
    with:
      message: "Hello from Loom!"
'
```

### Example: Upload a JSON workflow

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "name": "greet",
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "say_hello",
      "action": "echo",
      "with": {
        "message": "Hello from Loom!"
      }
    }
  ]
}'
```

The response includes the workflow's unique ID, which you'll need to start an execution:

```json
{
  "id": "wf_abc123",
  "name": "greet",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}
```

Save this ID — we'll use it in the next step.

---

## 3. Start an Execution

To run your workflow, send a `POST` to `/executions` with the workflow ID:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "workflow_id": "wf_abc123"
}'
```

The response returns the execution ID:

```json
{
  "id": "exec_xyz789",
  "workflow_id": "wf_abc123",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:00Z"
}
```

---

## 4. Check Execution Status

Poll `GET /executions/{id}` to check the current status of your execution:

```bash
curl https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions/exec_xyz789 \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here"
```

The response includes a `status` field. Loom v2.2 supports the following statuses:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queued` | The execution is waiting to start |
| `running` | The execution is in progress |
| `succeeded` | The execution completed successfully |
| `failed` | The execution completed with errors |
| `cancelled` | The execution was cancelled by the user |

Example response:

```json
{
  "id": "exec_xyz789",
  "workflow_id": "wf_abc123",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:00Z",
  "completed_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:05Z"
}
```

---

## 5. Set Up a Webhook

Instead of polling, you can configure a webhook to receive notifications when your execution finishes. Use `PUT /hooks` to subscribe to events:

```bash
curl -X PUT https://api.loom.sh/v2/hooks \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "url": "https://your-server.com/loom-webhook",
  "events": [
    "execution.succeeded",
    "execution.failed",
    "execution.cancelled"
  ]
}'
```

Loom v2.2 supports three webhook events:

| Event | Triggered when… |
|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | An execution completes successfully |
| `execution.failed` | An execution completes with errors |
| `execution.cancelled` | An execution is cancelled |

Each webhook payload includes the execution ID and status so you can look up full details.

---

## 6. Rate Limits

Loom enforces a rate limit of **120 requests per minute per API key** across all v2 endpoints. If you exceed this limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Design your polling and webhook retry logic accordingly.

---

## Recap

Here's what you've done:

1. ✅ Authenticated with an API key via the `X-Loom-Key` header
2. ✅ Uploaded a workflow definition (YAML or JSON) to `POST /workflows`
3. ✅ Started an execution with `POST /executions`
4. ✅ Checked the execution status with `GET /executions/{id}`
5. ✅ Learned the five possible statuses: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
6. ✅ Configured a webhook via `PUT /hooks` for `execution.succeeded`, `execution.failed`, and `execution.cancelled` events
7. ✅ Noted the rate limit of 120 requests/minute per key

You're ready to build with Loom. For the full endpoint reference, see the [API Reference](reference.md).

# Loom API v2.2 — Endpoint Reference

This document is the complete endpoint reference for the Loom workflow-orchestration HTTP API, version 2.2. All endpoints are relative to the base URL `https://api.loom.sh/v2`.

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Authentication](#authentication)
2. [Rate Limiting](#rate-limiting)
3. [Endpoints](#endpoints)
   - [Executions](#executions)
   - [Workflows](#workflows)
   - [Webhooks](#webhooks)
4. [Execution Statuses](#execution-statuses)
5. [Webhook Events](#webhook-events)
6. [Errors](#errors)

---

## Authentication

All v2 API requests require authentication via a scoped API key passed in the `X-Loom-Key` header.

```
X-Loom-Key: <your-api-key>
```

### Scoped API Keys

API keys are scoped to specific permissions. If a key lacks the scope required for a given endpoint, the server returns `403 Forbidden`.

### Legacy v1 Authentication

The v1 Bearer token scheme (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) is retained for backward compatibility, but **only** on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix. It does not work on any v2 endpoint.

### OAuth2

OAuth2 authentication is planned but has not shipped. It is not available in v2.2.

---

## Rate Limiting

All v2 endpoints share a unified rate limit of **120 requests per minute per API key**. The limit applies across all v2 endpoints.

When the rate limit is exceeded, the server returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header indicating the number of seconds to wait.

---

## Endpoints

### Executions

#### POST /executions

Start a new workflow execution.

**Request**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/json` |

**Request Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow_id` | string | Yes | The ID of the workflow definition to execute |
| `inputs` | object | No | Key-value pairs passed as inputs to the workflow |
| `metadata` | object | No | Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the execution |

**Example Request**

```http
POST /executions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "inputs": {
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "production"
  }
}
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|
| `201 Created` | Execution started successfully |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid request body or missing required fields |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (201)**

```json
{
  "id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "inputs": {
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "production"
  }
}
```

---

#### GET /executions/{id}

Retrieve details and current status of a specific execution.

**Path Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The execution ID |

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |

**Example Request**

```http
GET /executions/exec_7f3a9b2c HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Execution found |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `404 Not Found` | Execution does not exist |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "running",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "started_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:05Z",
  "inputs": {
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "production"
  },
  "outputs": null
}
```

The `status` field is one of: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

---

#### POST /executions/{id}/cancel

Cancel a running or queued execution.

**Path Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The execution ID |

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |

**Example Request**

```http
POST /executions/exec_7f3a9b2c/cancel HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Execution cancelled successfully |
| `400 Bad Request` | Execution cannot be cancelled (e.g., already completed) |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `404 Not Found` | Execution does not exist |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "cancelled",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "started_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:05Z",
  "cancelled_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:22Z"
}
```

---

### Workflows

#### POST /workflows

Upload a workflow definition. Both YAML and JSON formats are accepted.

**Request**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/x-yaml` for YAML, `application/json` for JSON |

**Request Body**

The request body is the workflow definition itself. The maximum size is **1 MB**.

**Example Request (YAML)**

```http
POST /workflows HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/x-yaml

name: deploy-prod
version: 1
steps:
  - id: build
    type: shell
    command: make build
  - id: deploy
    type: shell
    command: make deploy
    depends_on: [build]
```

**Example Request (JSON)**

```http
POST /workflows HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "deploy-prod",
  "version": 1,
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "build",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "make build"
    },
    {
      "id": "deploy",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "make deploy",
      "depends_on": ["build"]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `201 Created` | Workflow definition uploaded successfully |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid definition format or content |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `413 Payload Too Large` | Definition exceeds 1 MB limit |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (201)**

```json
{
  "id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "name": "deploy-prod",
  "version": 1,
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T09:00:00Z"
}
```

---

#### GET /workflows/{id}/versions

List all definition versions for a workflow.

**Path Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The workflow ID |

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |

**Example Request**

```http
GET /workflows/wf_deploy-prod/versions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Versions listed successfully |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `404 Not Found` | Workflow does not exist |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "versions": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T09:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "version": 2,
      "created_at": "2025-01-16T14:22:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Webhooks

#### PUT /hooks

Configure webhook subscriptions for execution events.

**Request**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/json` |

**Request Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | Yes | The HTTPS URL to receive webhook payloads |
| `events` | array | Yes | List of event names to subscribe to |

**Supported event names**: `execution.succeeded`, `execution.failed`, `execution.cancelled`.

**Example Request**

```http
PUT /hooks HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://myapp.example.com/webhooks/loom",
  "events": ["execution.succeeded", "execution.failed", "execution.cancelled"]
}
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Webhook configuration updated |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid URL or unrecognized event names |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "url": "https://myapp.example.com/webhooks/loom",
  "events": ["execution.succeeded", "execution.failed", "execution.cancelled"],
  "updated_at": "2025-01-15T11:00:00Z"
}
```

**Webhook Payload**

When an event fires, Loom sends a `POST` request to the configured URL with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "event": "execution.succeeded",
  "execution_id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "completed_at": "2025-01-15T10:35:00Z"
}
```

---

## Execution Statuses

The `status` field on an execution object takes one of the following values:

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| `queued` | The execution is waiting to start |
| `running` | The execution is in progress |
| `succeeded` | The execution completed successfully |
| `failed` | The execution completed with errors |
| `cancelled` | The execution was cancelled by the user via `POST /executions/{id}/cancel` |

---

## Webhook Events

Loom sends webhook notifications for the following events:

| Event Name | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | An execution completed successfully (status: `succeeded`) |
| `execution.failed` | An execution completed with errors (status: `failed`) |
| `execution.cancelled` | An execution was cancelled (status: `cancelled`) |

---

## Errors

All error responses use a consistent JSON format:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "message": "The workflow_id field is required."
  }
}
```

| HTTP Status | Error Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `invalid_request` | The request body is malformed or missing required fields |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | The `X-Loom-Key` header is missing or contains an invalid key |
| `403` | `forbidden` | The API key does not have the required scope for this operation |
| `404` | `not_found` | The requested resource does not exist |
| `413` | `payload_too_large` | The request body exceeds the 1 MB limit |
| `429` | `rate_limit_exceeded` | The rate limit of 120 requests/minute has been exceeded |

# Loom API v2.2 — Canonical API Inventory

This document is the single source of truth for the Loom API v2.2 surface. All documentation must match this inventory exactly. Each section records the reconciliation decision and its justification.

---

## 1. Base URL & Versioning

- **Base URL**: `https://api.loom.sh/v2`
- **Version**: 2.2 (current)
- **Legacy prefix**: `/v1/*` still accepts v1-style requests with Bearer authentication.

---

## 2. Authentication

| Aspect | Value | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Header | `X-Loom-Key` | F3, F4 | Scoped API keys passed in this header |
| OAuth2 | Not available | F3 | Planned but has not shipped |
| v1 Legacy | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on `/v1/*` | F4 | Only works on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix |

**Reconciliation**: F3 and F4 are consistent. v2 authentication uses the `X-Loom-Key` header with scoped API keys. The v1 Bearer token scheme is retained only for backward compatibility on the `/v1/*` prefix.

---

## 3. Endpoints

### 3.1 Executions

| Method | Path | Description | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/executions` | Start a workflow execution | F1 |
| `GET` | `/executions/{id}` | Get execution details and status | F5 |
| `POST` | `/executions/{id}/cancel` | Cancel a running or queued execution | F6 |

**Reconciliation — `/run` alias**: F1 (2.0 notes) stated the old `/run` endpoint would remain as a deprecated alias until 2.2. However, F2 (2.1 changelog) states it was removed ahead of schedule due to CVE-2025-1188. The 2.1 changelog is the later, more specific source. **Decision**: `/run` is NOT available in v2.2.

### 3.2 Workflows

| Method | Path | Description | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/workflows` | Upload a workflow definition | F11, F12 |
| `GET` | `/workflows/{id}/versions` | List definition versions for a workflow | F12 |

### 3.3 Webhooks

| Method | Path | Description | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PUT` | `/hooks` | Configure webhook subscriptions | F8 |

---

## 4. Execution Statuses

| Status | Description | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `queued` | Execution is waiting to start | F5 |
| `running` | Execution is in progress | F5 |
| `succeeded` | Execution completed successfully | F5 |
| `failed` | Execution completed with errors | F5 |
| `cancelled` | Execution was cancelled by the user | F6 |

**Reconciliation**: F5 lists the original four statuses from v2.0. F6 (2.2 changelog) adds `cancelled`. All five are current.

---

## 5. Webhook Events

| Event Name | Trigger | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | Execution completed successfully | F9 |
| `execution.failed` | Execution completed with errors | F8, F9 |
| `execution.cancelled` | Execution was cancelled | F10 |

**Reconciliation**: F8 (2.0) listed `execution.finished` and `execution.failed`. F9 (2.1) renamed `execution.finished` → `execution.succeeded` and removed `execution.finished`. F10 (support ticket) confirms `execution.cancelled` was added silently in 2.2. Current events: `execution.succeeded`, `execution.failed`, `execution.cancelled`.

---

## 6. Workflow Definitions

| Aspect | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted formats | YAML, JSON | F12 |
| Maximum size | 1 MB | F12 |
| Upload endpoint | `POST /workflows` | F11, F12 |

**Reconciliation**: F11 (2.0) specified YAML only at 512 KB. F12 (2.2) adds JSON support and raises the limit to 1 MB. F12 supersedes.

---

## 7. Rate Limiting

| Aspect | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Limit | 120 requests/minute per API key | F6 |
| Scope | All v2 endpoints | F7 (scope), F6 (value) |

**Reconciliation**: F6 (2.2 changelog) states the limit was raised from 60 to 120 requests/min. F7 (undated internal memo) states 100 requests/min. F6 is the official, dated changelog entry for the current version and is more authoritative than an undated memo. **Decision**: 120 requests/min per key.

---

## 8. Source Fragment Index

| ID | Type | Version | Key Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Release notes | 2.0 | `/run` → `/executions` rename, `/run` deprecated alias |
| F2 | Changelog | 2.1 | `/run` alias removed (CVE-2025-1188) |
| F3 | Launch blog | 2.0 | X-Loom-Key auth, OAuth2 planned |
| F4 | Support ticket | 2.1 | Confirms X-Loom-Key for v2, Bearer for v1 legacy |
| F5 | Release notes | 2.0 | Execution statuses: queued, running, succeeded, failed |
| F6 | Changelog | 2.2 | Added `cancelled` status, cancel endpoint, rate limit 120/min |
| F7 | Internal memo | undated | Rate limit 100/min (superseded by F6) |
| F8 | Release notes | 2.0 | Webhooks via PUT /hooks, events: execution.finished, execution.failed |
| F9 | Changelog | 2.1 | execution.succeeded replaces execution.finished |
| F10 | Support ticket | 2.2 | execution.cancelled webhook added silently |
| F11 | Release notes | 2.0 | YAML workflows, 512 KB limit |
| F12 | Changelog | 2.2 | JSON+YAML workflows, 1 MB limit, GET /workflows/{id}/versions |

# Loom API v1 → v2.2 Migration Guide

This guide walks existing Loom API v1 users through every change required to migrate to v2.2. Each section shows the v1 behavior, the v2.2 behavior, and actionable code examples.

**Base URL**: `https://api.loom.sh/v2`

---

## 1. Authentication

### What changed

| | v1 | v2.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Header | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `X-Loom-Key: <api-key>` |
| Key type | Bearer token | Scoped API key |

v2 uses scoped API keys passed in the `X-Loom-Key` header. OAuth2 was planned but has **not shipped** — do not wait for it; use API keys.

The v1 Bearer scheme still works, but **only** on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix. This is a compatibility shim, not a recommendation for new code.

### Before (v1)

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v1/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"workflow_id": "wf_abc123"}'
```

### After (v2.2)

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"workflow_id": "wf_abc123"}'
```

### Action items

1. Generate a scoped API key in your Loom dashboard.
2. Replace every `Authorization: Bearer` header with `X-Loom-Key`.
3. Update your base URL from `/v1` to `/v2`.

---

## 2. Endpoint Rename: `/run` → `/executions`

### What changed

The v1 `POST /run` endpoint was renamed to `POST /executions` in v2.0. The `/run` alias was originally planned to persist until v2.2 but was **removed in v2.1** due to CVE-2025-1188. It is **not available** in v2.2.

| | v1 | v2.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Start execution | `POST /run` | `POST /executions` |
| Get execution | `GET /run/{id}` | `GET /executions/{id}` |

### Before (v1)

```bash
# Start a workflow
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v1/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"workflow_id": "wf_abc123"}'

# Check status
curl https://api.loom.sh/v1/run/exec_789 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

### After (v2.2)

```bash
# Start a workflow
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>" \
  -d '{"workflow_id": "wf_abc123"}'

# Check status
curl https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions/exec_789 \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>"
```

### Action items

1. Replace all references to `/run` with `/executions` in your codebase.
2. Do **not** rely on the `/run` alias — it no longer exists.

---

## 3. Webhook Event Rename: `execution.finished` → `execution.succeeded`

### What changed

In v2.1, webhook event names were normalized. `execution.finished` was **replaced** by `execution.succeeded`. The old event name is no longer delivered.

| | v1 / v2.0 | v2.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Success event | `execution.finished` | `execution.succeeded` |
| Failure event | `execution.failed` | `execution.failed` (unchanged) |

### Before (v2.0)

```python
def handle_webhook(event):
    if event["type"] == "execution.finished":
        log_success(event["execution_id"])
    elif event["type"] == "execution.failed":
        log_failure(event["execution_id"])
```

### After (v2.2)

```python
def handle_webhook(event):
    if event["type"] == "execution.succeeded":
        log_success(event["execution_id"])
    elif event["type"] == "execution.failed":
        log_failure(event["execution_id"])
    elif event["type"] == "execution.cancelled":
        log_cancelled(event["execution_id"])
```

### Action items

1. Update webhook handlers to listen for `execution.succeeded` instead of `execution.finished`.
2. Update your webhook subscription via `PUT /hooks` to use the new event name.

---

## 4. New Webhook Event: `execution.cancelled`

### What changed

v2.2 added the `execution.cancelled` webhook event alongside the new cancel endpoint. It was added silently in 2.2 and is now documented.

### Current webhook events in v2.2

| Event | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | Execution completed successfully |
| `execution.failed` | Execution completed with errors |
| `execution.cancelled` | Execution was cancelled by the user |

### Example: Subscribe to all events

```bash
curl -X PUT https://api.loom.sh/v2/hooks \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://my-app.example.com/webhooks/loom",
    "events": ["execution.succeeded", "execution.failed", "execution.cancelled"]
  }'
```

### Action items

1. Decide whether your application should handle `execution.cancelled` events.
2. If yes, add a handler and include the event in your `PUT /hooks` subscription.

---

## 5. New Execution Status: `cancelled`

### What changed

v2.2 added a `cancelled` status. If your code polls `GET /executions/{id}` for terminal states, you must now handle `cancelled` alongside `succeeded` and `failed`.

### Current statuses in v2.2

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queued` | Execution is waiting to start |
| `running` | Execution is in progress |
| `succeeded` | Execution completed successfully |
| `failed` | Execution completed with errors |
| `cancelled` | Execution was cancelled by the user |

### Before (v2.0)

```python
status = response["status"]
if status in ("succeeded", "failed"):
    # terminal state
    process_result(status)
```

### After (v2.2)

```python
status = response["status"]
if status in ("succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"):
    # terminal state
    process_result(status)
```

### Action items

1. Add `cancelled` to your set of terminal statuses in polling logic.
2. Decide how your application should respond to a cancelled execution.

---

## 6. New Cancel Endpoint: `POST /executions/{id}/cancel`

### What changed

v2.2 added the ability to cancel a running or queued execution.

### Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions/exec_789/cancel \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>"
```

### Action items

1. If your application needs to stop in-progress workflows, integrate this endpoint.
2. After cancelling, poll `GET /executions/{id}` or listen for the `execution.cancelled` webhook to confirm the status changed to `cancelled`.

---

## 7. Workflow Definition Changes

### What changed

| | v1 / v2.0 | v2.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted formats | YAML only | YAML **and** JSON |
| Maximum size | 512 KB | 1 MB |

### Before (v2.0 — YAML only)

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-yaml" \
  --data-binary @workflow.yaml
```

### After (v2.2 — JSON also accepted)

```bash
# YAML still works
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-yaml" \
  --data-binary @workflow.yaml

# JSON is now also accepted
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @workflow.json
```

### Action items

1. If you were constrained by the 512 KB limit, you can now upload definitions up to 1 MB.
2. If your toolchain produces JSON, you can now upload directly without converting to YAML.

---

## 8. New Endpoint: `GET /workflows/{id}/versions`

### What changed

v2.2 added an endpoint to list definition versions for a workflow.

### Example

```bash
curl https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows/wf_abc123/versions \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: <api-key>"
```

### Action items

1. If you need to track or roll back workflow definition changes, integrate this endpoint.

---

## 9. Rate Limit Change

### What changed

The v2.2 rate limit is **120 requests per minute per API key**, across all v2 endpoints. This is an increase from the v2.0 limit of 60 requests/min.

| | v2.0 | v2.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Rate limit | 60 req/min per key | 120 req/min per key |

### Action items

1. If you implemented rate-limit backoff tuned to 60 req/min, you can relax it to 120 req/min.
2. Monitor `429` responses; the limit is enforced per API key across all v2 endpoints.

---

## 10. OAuth2 — Not Available

OAuth2 support was announced as planned but has **not shipped**. Do not block your migration waiting for OAuth2. Use scoped API keys via the `X-Loom-Key` header.

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

- [ ] Replace `Authorization: Bearer` with `X-Loom-Key` header.
- [ ] Update base URL from `/v1` to `/v2`.
- [ ] Replace all `/run` references with `/executions`.
- [ ] Replace `execution.finished` webhook event with `execution.succeeded`.
- [ ] Add handler for `execution.cancelled` webhook event (optional but recommended).
- [ ] Add `cancelled` to terminal statuses in polling logic.
- [ ] Update webhook subscriptions via `PUT /hooks` with current event names.
- [ ] Review workflow definition size — limit is now 1 MB (was 512 KB).
- [ ] Consider using JSON format for workflow definitions (now supported).
- [ ] Use `GET /workflows/{id}/versions` to track definition history (optional).
- [ ] Use `POST /executions/{id}/cancel` to cancel executions (optional).
- [ ] Adjust rate-limit backoff to 120 req/min per key.
- [ ] Do **not** wait for OAuth2 — use API keys.

# Loom API v2.2 — Troubleshooting FAQ

This FAQ addresses common issues, gotchas, and edge cases when using the Loom API v2.2. Every answer is reconciled against the [canonical API inventory](inventory.md).

---

## 1. I'm getting 401 errors with my Bearer token

**Problem:** You are sending `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to a v2 endpoint and receiving a 401 Unauthorized response.

**Cause:** Loom v2 does **not** use the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Authentication for all v2 endpoints uses scoped API keys passed in the `X-Loom-Key` header.

**Fix:** Replace your authentication header:

```http
# Wrong (v1 style — does not work on v2 endpoints)
Authorization: Bearer <your-token>

# Correct (v2)
X-Loom-Key: <your-api-key>
```

**Note:** The v1 Bearer token scheme still works, but **only** on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix. If you need to use Bearer tokens, route your requests to `https://api.loom.sh/v1/...` instead. New development should target v2 with `X-Loom-Key`.

---

## 2. The /run endpoint returns 404

**Problem:** `POST /run` (or any request to `/run`) returns a 404 Not Found.

**Cause:** The `/run` endpoint was renamed to `/executions` in v2.0. A deprecated `/run` alias was originally planned to remain available until v2.2, but it was **removed ahead of schedule in v2.1** due to a security vulnerability (CVE-2025-1188). The alias does not exist in v2.2.

**Fix:** Use `POST /executions` to start a workflow execution:

```http
POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions
X-Loom-Key: <your-api-key>
Content-Type: application/yaml

<workflow-definition>
```

---

## 3. I'm not receiving execution.finished webhooks

**Problem:** Your webhook handler expects `execution.finished` events but never receives them.

**Cause:** The `execution.finished` event name was **renamed to `execution.succeeded`** in v2.1 as part of a webhook event name normalization. The old `execution.finished` event was removed entirely.

**Fix:** Update your webhook subscription via `PUT /hooks` to listen for `execution.succeeded` instead:

```json
{
  "events": ["execution.succeeded", "execution.failed"]
}
```

---

## 4. What webhook events are available?

The following webhook events are available in v2.2. Configure them via `PUT /hooks`:

| Event | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | An execution completed successfully |
| `execution.failed` | An execution completed with errors |
| `execution.cancelled` | An execution was cancelled by the user |

**Note:** `execution.cancelled` was added in v2.2 alongside the cancel endpoint. It was added silently and may not appear in older documentation. If you are not receiving cancellation notifications, add `execution.cancelled` to your webhook subscription.

---

## 5. My workflow upload is rejected as too large

**Problem:** `POST /workflows` returns an error indicating the payload exceeds the maximum size.

**Cause:** The maximum workflow definition size is **1 MB**. If you are seeing rejections at 512 KB, you may be referencing outdated v2.0 documentation — the limit was raised from 512 KB to 1 MB in v2.2.

**Fix:**
- Ensure your workflow definition is under 1 MB.
- Both **YAML** and **JSON** formats are accepted (JSON support was added in v2.2). Set the appropriate `Content-Type` header:
  - `application/yaml` for YAML definitions
  - `application/json` for JSON definitions

---

## 6. I'm hitting rate limits

**Problem:** You are receiving 429 Too Many Requests responses.

**Cause:** The rate limit is **120 requests per minute per API key**, applied across all v2 endpoints.

**Note:** Some older sources (including an undated internal memo) may state the limit is 100 requests/minute. The authoritative value from the v2.2 changelog is **120 requests/minute**. If you were previously limited to 60/min (v2.0), the limit was raised in v2.2.

**Fix:**
- Throttle your client to stay under 120 requests/minute per key.
- If you need higher throughput, consider using multiple API keys.

---

## 7. Can I use OAuth2?

**Answer:** No. OAuth2 support is **planned but has not shipped**. The only supported authentication method for v2 endpoints is scoped API keys via the `X-Loom-Key` header.

If you require OAuth2, monitor the Loom changelog for future announcements. In the meantime, use `X-Loom-Key` authentication.

---

## 8. What does the cancelled status mean?

**Answer:** The `cancelled` execution status was added in v2.2. It indicates that an execution was cancelled by the user before it completed.

**How to cancel an execution:**

```http
POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions/{id}/cancel
X-Loom-Key: <your-api-key>
```

This endpoint cancels a running or queued execution. After cancellation:
- `GET /executions/{id}` will return `"status": "cancelled"`.
- An `execution.cancelled` webhook event is emitted (if subscribed).

The full set of execution statuses in v2.2 is: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

---

## 9. How do I list versions of a workflow definition?

**Answer:** Use the `GET /workflows/{id}/versions` endpoint, added in v2.2:

```http
GET https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows/{id}/versions
X-Loom-Key: <your-api-key>
```

This returns a list of all definition versions for the specified workflow. This endpoint did not exist before v2.2.

---

## 10. Is the /v1/* prefix still supported?

**Answer:** Yes. The `/v1/*` legacy prefix is still supported for backward compatibility. It accepts v1-style requests with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` authentication.

**Important:** The v1 prefix is maintained for legacy integrations only. New development should target the v2 API (`https://api.loom.sh/v2`) with `X-Loom-Key` authentication. The v1 prefix may be deprecated in a future major release.

---

## Quick Reference: Common Mistakes

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 on v2 endpoints | Using `Authorization: Bearer` | Switch to `X-Loom-Key` header |
| 404 on `/run` | Endpoint was removed in v2.1 | Use `POST /executions` |
| No `execution.finished` webhooks | Event renamed in v2.1 | Subscribe to `execution.succeeded` |
| 429 rate limit errors | Exceeding 120 req/min per key | Throttle requests or use more keys |
| Workflow upload rejected | Payload > 1 MB | Reduce definition size |
| Missing cancellation notifications | Not subscribed to `execution.cancelled` | Add event to webhook config |

---

# Getting Started with Loom API v2.2

Welcome to Loom! This guide will walk you through making your first workflow execution using the Loom HTTP API. By the end, you'll have uploaded a workflow definition, started an execution, checked its status, and set up a webhook to receive completion notifications.

All examples use `curl` against the Loom API base URL:

```
https://api.loom.sh/v2
```

---

## 1. Get an API Key

Loom uses **scoped API keys** for authentication. Obtain a key from your Loom dashboard (or contact your administrator). You'll pass it in the `X-Loom-Key` header on every request.

> **Note:** OAuth2 support is planned but has not shipped yet. For now, API keys are the only authentication method for v2.

> **Legacy note:** If you're migrating from v1, the old `Authorization: Bearer <token>` scheme still works, but only on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix. For v2 endpoints, always use `X-Loom-Key`.

---

## 2. Upload a Workflow Definition

Workflows are defined as YAML or JSON documents and uploaded via `POST /workflows`. The maximum definition size is **1 MB**.

### Example: Upload a YAML workflow

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-yaml" \
  -d '
name: greet
steps:
  - id: say_hello
    action: echo
    with:
      message: "Hello from Loom!"
'
```

### Example: Upload a JSON workflow

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/workflows \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "name": "greet",
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "say_hello",
      "action": "echo",
      "with": {
        "message": "Hello from Loom!"
      }
    }
  ]
}'
```

The response includes the workflow's unique ID, which you'll need to start an execution:

```json
{
  "id": "wf_abc123",
  "name": "greet",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}
```

Save this ID — we'll use it in the next step.

---

## 3. Start an Execution

To run your workflow, send a `POST` to `/executions` with the workflow ID:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "workflow_id": "wf_abc123"
}'
```

The response returns the execution ID:

```json
{
  "id": "exec_xyz789",
  "workflow_id": "wf_abc123",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:00Z"
}
```

---

## 4. Check Execution Status

Poll `GET /executions/{id}` to check the current status of your execution:

```bash
curl https://api.loom.sh/v2/executions/exec_xyz789 \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here"
```

The response includes a `status` field. Loom v2.2 supports the following statuses:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queued` | The execution is waiting to start |
| `running` | The execution is in progress |
| `succeeded` | The execution completed successfully |
| `failed` | The execution completed with errors |
| `cancelled` | The execution was cancelled by the user |

Example response:

```json
{
  "id": "exec_xyz789",
  "workflow_id": "wf_abc123",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:00Z",
  "completed_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:05Z"
}
```

---

## 5. Set Up a Webhook

Instead of polling, you can configure a webhook to receive notifications when your execution finishes. Use `PUT /hooks` to subscribe to events:

```bash
curl -X PUT https://api.loom.sh/v2/hooks \
  -H "X-Loom-Key: your-api-key-here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "url": "https://your-server.com/loom-webhook",
  "events": [
    "execution.succeeded",
    "execution.failed",
    "execution.cancelled"
  ]
}'
```

Loom v2.2 supports three webhook events:

| Event | Triggered when… |
|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | An execution completes successfully |
| `execution.failed` | An execution completes with errors |
| `execution.cancelled` | An execution is cancelled |

Each webhook payload includes the execution ID and status so you can look up full details.

---

## 6. Rate Limits

Loom enforces a rate limit of **120 requests per minute per API key** across all v2 endpoints. If you exceed this limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Design your polling and webhook retry logic accordingly.

---

## Recap

Here's what you've done:

1. ✅ Authenticated with an API key via the `X-Loom-Key` header
2. ✅ Uploaded a workflow definition (YAML or JSON) to `POST /workflows`
3. ✅ Started an execution with `POST /executions`
4. ✅ Checked the execution status with `GET /executions/{id}`
5. ✅ Learned the five possible statuses: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
6. ✅ Configured a webhook via `PUT /hooks` for `execution.succeeded`, `execution.failed`, and `execution.cancelled` events
7. ✅ Noted the rate limit of 120 requests/minute per key

You're ready to build with Loom. For the full endpoint reference, see the [API Reference](reference.md).

# Loom API v2.2 — Endpoint Reference

This document is the complete endpoint reference for the Loom workflow-orchestration HTTP API, version 2.2. All endpoints are relative to the base URL `https://api.loom.sh/v2`.

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Authentication](#authentication)
2. [Rate Limiting](#rate-limiting)
3. [Endpoints](#endpoints)
   - [Executions](#executions)
   - [Workflows](#workflows)
   - [Webhooks](#webhooks)
4. [Execution Statuses](#execution-statuses)
5. [Webhook Events](#webhook-events)
6. [Errors](#errors)

---

## Authentication

All v2 API requests require authentication via a scoped API key passed in the `X-Loom-Key` header.

```
X-Loom-Key: <your-api-key>
```

### Scoped API Keys

API keys are scoped to specific permissions. If a key lacks the scope required for a given endpoint, the server returns `403 Forbidden`.

### Legacy v1 Authentication

The v1 Bearer token scheme (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) is retained for backward compatibility, but **only** on the `/v1/*` legacy prefix. It does not work on any v2 endpoint.

### OAuth2

OAuth2 authentication is planned but has not shipped. It is not available in v2.2.

---

## Rate Limiting

All v2 endpoints share a unified rate limit of **120 requests per minute per API key**. The limit applies across all v2 endpoints.

When the rate limit is exceeded, the server returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header indicating the number of seconds to wait.

---

## Endpoints

### Executions

#### POST /executions

Start a new workflow execution.

**Request**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/json` |

**Request Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow_id` | string | Yes | The ID of the workflow definition to execute |
| `inputs` | object | No | Key-value pairs passed as inputs to the workflow |
| `metadata` | object | No | Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the execution |

**Example Request**

```http
POST /executions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "inputs": {
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "production"
  }
}
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|
| `201 Created` | Execution started successfully |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid request body or missing required fields |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (201)**

```json
{
  "id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "inputs": {
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "production"
  }
}
```

---

#### GET /executions/{id}

Retrieve details and current status of a specific execution.

**Path Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The execution ID |

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |

**Example Request**

```http
GET /executions/exec_7f3a9b2c HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Execution found |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `404 Not Found` | Execution does not exist |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "running",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "started_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:05Z",
  "inputs": {
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "production"
  },
  "outputs": null
}
```

The `status` field is one of: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

---

#### POST /executions/{id}/cancel

Cancel a running or queued execution.

**Path Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The execution ID |

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |

**Example Request**

```http
POST /executions/exec_7f3a9b2c/cancel HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Execution cancelled successfully |
| `400 Bad Request` | Execution cannot be cancelled (e.g., already completed) |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `404 Not Found` | Execution does not exist |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "cancelled",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "started_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:05Z",
  "cancelled_at": "2025-01-15T10:31:22Z"
}
```

---

### Workflows

#### POST /workflows

Upload a workflow definition. Both YAML and JSON formats are accepted.

**Request**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/x-yaml` for YAML, `application/json` for JSON |

**Request Body**

The request body is the workflow definition itself. The maximum size is **1 MB**.

**Example Request (YAML)**

```http
POST /workflows HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/x-yaml

name: deploy-prod
version: 1
steps:
  - id: build
    type: shell
    command: make build
  - id: deploy
    type: shell
    command: make deploy
    depends_on: [build]
```

**Example Request (JSON)**

```http
POST /workflows HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "deploy-prod",
  "version": 1,
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "build",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "make build"
    },
    {
      "id": "deploy",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "make deploy",
      "depends_on": ["build"]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `201 Created` | Workflow definition uploaded successfully |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid definition format or content |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `413 Payload Too Large` | Definition exceeds 1 MB limit |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (201)**

```json
{
  "id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "name": "deploy-prod",
  "version": 1,
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T09:00:00Z"
}
```

---

#### GET /workflows/{id}/versions

List all definition versions for a workflow.

**Path Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The workflow ID |

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |

**Example Request**

```http
GET /workflows/wf_deploy-prod/versions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Versions listed successfully |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `404 Not Found` | Workflow does not exist |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "versions": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T09:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "version": 2,
      "created_at": "2025-01-16T14:22:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Webhooks

#### PUT /hooks

Configure webhook subscriptions for execution events.

**Request**

| Header | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Loom-Key` | Yes | Scoped API key |
| `Content-Type` | Yes | `application/json` |

**Request Body**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | Yes | The HTTPS URL to receive webhook payloads |
| `events` | array | Yes | List of event names to subscribe to |

**Supported event names**: `execution.succeeded`, `execution.failed`, `execution.cancelled`.

**Example Request**

```http
PUT /hooks HTTP/1.1
Host: api.loom.sh
X-Loom-Key: lkm_abc123
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://myapp.example.com/webhooks/loom",
  "events": ["execution.succeeded", "execution.failed", "execution.cancelled"]
}
```

**Response**

| Status Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Webhook configuration updated |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid URL or unrecognized event names |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key lacks required scope |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example Response (200)**

```json
{
  "url": "https://myapp.example.com/webhooks/loom",
  "events": ["execution.succeeded", "execution.failed", "execution.cancelled"],
  "updated_at": "2025-01-15T11:00:00Z"
}
```

**Webhook Payload**

When an event fires, Loom sends a `POST` request to the configured URL with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "event": "execution.succeeded",
  "execution_id": "exec_7f3a9b2c",
  "workflow_id": "wf_deploy-prod",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "completed_at": "2025-01-15T10:35:00Z"
}
```

---

## Execution Statuses

The `status` field on an execution object takes one of the following values:

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| `queued` | The execution is waiting to start |
| `running` | The execution is in progress |
| `succeeded` | The execution completed successfully |
| `failed` | The execution completed with errors |
| `cancelled` | The execution was cancelled by the user via `POST /executions/{id}/cancel` |

---

## Webhook Events

Loom sends webhook notifications for the following events:

| Event Name | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `execution.succeeded` | An execution completed successfully (status: `succeeded`) |
| `execution.failed` | An execution completed with errors (status: `failed`) |
| `execution.cancelled` | An execution was cancelled (status: `cancelled`) |

---

## Errors

All error responses use a consistent JSON format:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "message": "The workflow_id field is required."
  }
}
```

| HTTP Status | Error Code | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `invalid_request` | The request body is malformed or missing required fields |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | The `X-Loom-Key` header is missing or contains an invalid key |
| `403` | `forbidden` | The API key does not have the required scope for this operation |
| `404` | `not_found` | The requested resource does not exist |
| `413` | `payload_too_large` | The request body exceeds the 1 MB limit |
| `429` | `rate_limit_exceeded` | The rate limit of 120 requests/minute has been exceeded |
